A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ColPali and ViDoRe. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renamed material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval evaluations, latency measurements, training ablations, and qualitative similarity-map analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical evaluations and adds token-pooling experiments, DocMatix-only training, and a Qwen2-based retrieval variant.

M1.justification: v4 adds optional hierarchical mean token pooling to compress document representations and introduces the Qwen2-VL-based ColQwen2 variant. These extend the method while retaining the original ColPali architecture, late-interaction scoring, pairwise objective, and query augmentation.

E1.justification: Section 6 adds training on DocMatix, described as a separate document-QA distribution, to evaluate transfer to ViDoRe. The ten evaluation datasets, English/French coverage, and page-retrieval tasks remain unchanged; expanded dataset descriptions do not establish additional benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: ColQwen2 is added to the architectural comparison in Section 6 and Table 7. The principal BM25, BGE-M3, Jina-CLIP, Nomic-vision, SigLIP, and existing model-variant comparisons are retained. Previously plotted ablations appearing in the expanded table are not new comparator families.

E3.justification: New protocols include the pooling-factor sweep, a comparably sized DocMatix-only training control, and Qwen2 evaluation with a 768-patch limit. The reported main training-set size changes from 127,460 to 118,695. Latency sampling changes from a 100-page document in v3 Appendix B.5 to 1,000 randomly selected documents in v4 Appendix B.4, although v4's main-text footnote still says 100 pages. These reporting changes do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 substantially extends analysis with compression-versus-accuracy curves, a disjoint-training-distribution control, and a newer-backbone comparison. Table 7 also supplies dataset-level breakdowns for existing ablations previously summarized graphically or verbally. Conversely, v3's healthcare molecular-structure similarity-map case study is removed; the other principal interpretability examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports retrieval-run seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The sparse-BM25 storage mean and standard deviation, 1.56 ± 0.51 KB, are retained in v3 Table 3 and v4 Table 4.

E6.justification: The main nDCG@5 and Recall@1 tables retain their numerical entries. Added results include average nDCG@5 of 79.1 for DocMatix-trained ColPali and 86.6 for ColQwen2, versus the retained ColPali reference of 81.3, under different training or backbone configurations. Pooling retains a reported 97.8% of performance with 66.7% fewer vectors. Dataset-level ablation results expand substantially, and the reported ColPali footprint changes from 256 to 257.5 KB.

T1.justification: v4 consolidates the loss formulation in Section 4.1, removing v3 Appendix B.2's inconsistent reversed positive score LI(d_k,q_k) and undefined negative-document symbol p_l. The consolidated formulation consistently uses LI(q_k,d_k) and d_l. This is a limited formal correction; the late-interaction operator and softplus objective remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain ViDoRe and an end-to-end visual late-interaction retriever claimed to outperform the evaluated conventional pipelines while enabling faster indexing and low query latency. The 'Retrieval in Vision Space' terminology reframes the existing concept; the new experiments support rather than replace these core claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations about redundant patches, greater pooling sensitivity in text-dense documents, backbone quality, and generalization beyond the training distribution. It removes v3's explicit limitations concerning PDF-focused coverage, high-resource languages, synthetic-query bias, and vector-database support. Abstention remains as future work, so that discussion is relocated rather than wholly deleted.

D1.justification: v4 adds training-mixture counts, explicit training-data access, VM and dtype details, no-gradient-accumulation disclosure, and the six document-prompt tokens explaining storage overhead. Its reproducibility statement specifies MIT-licensed adapters and other resources, replacing v3's base-model-license discussion. Mi250x training-cost disclosures disappear. Documentation improves in scope but contains inconsistencies: Table 3's component counts sum to 118,728 rather than its stated 118,695.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 newly acknowledges specialized table and chart retrieval work and qualifies benchmark novelty around practical, end-to-end evaluation across document types. Citations are added for token pooling, DocMatix, Qwen2-VL, and newer embedding research, while the principal intellectual foundations remain. The Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning citation is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, performance narrative, and ablation presentation receive substantial rewriting. The loss explanation moves into the main text, results and similarity-map appendices exchange order, and a model glossary and reproducibility statement are introduced. Dedicated limitations and ethical-considerations sections disappear, substantially changing the document's organization and emphasis.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR format. v4 restructures the dataset table, adds training-mixture and latency tables, expands the ablation table, and combines a new pooling plot with the relocated introductory heatmap. The earlier ablation bar chart and healthcare heatmap are removed; other figures and benchmark examples are retained with changed placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: The DocMatix control and pooling study strengthen evidence about training-distribution dependence and practical storage tradeoffs, while fuller ablation breakdowns improve scrutiny. These provide a modest net improvement despite unchanged principal results. The gains are tempered by removal of substantive limitations and compute-cost disclosures, plus inconsistent latency sample counts and training-mixture totals in the new documentation.
